topic.title: We binge it and forget its name
topic.claim: Dropping a full season at once made us finish shows faster and forget them faster; the shows people still talk about are the ones they waited for.
topic.moment: You finish a whole series over a weekend and a month later can't remember what it was called.

turn.believed: Binge release is better because you get everything at once.
turn.actually: Without the weekly wait, a show never gets weeks of chat around it, so it fades.

topic.feeling: Empty, like I ate a whole packet and didn't taste it.
topic.villain: Release models built to make people subscribe and finish fast.
topic.because: Platforms want you to finish and stay subscribed, not to discuss. But talk is what makes a show last, and talk needs gaps.
topic.payoff: Think of the last three shows you binged. Now think of one you waited a week for. Which one do you still quote?
topic.behaviour: Viewers binge whole seasons in a weekend and rarely discuss them afterwards.
topic.mechanism: Fast release removes the time that conversation needs.
topic.group: OTT subscribers in their 20s and early 30s
topic.send_to: The friend who recommended a show you can't remember finishing.
topic.why_now: Some platforms are moving back to weekly episodes, and it changes how shows are remembered.

score.why: Binge release means finishing shows and forgetting them. The talk that makes a show last needs gaps.
